limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/flow-worktree-sweep.sh reports `removable` for a worktree that meets all five of its conditions (PR merged, tree clean, nothing unpushed, no live process inside, not locked), and does NOT for five neighbours that each break exactly one: a dirty tree, a local commit beyond the head GitHub merged, a process inside the worktree, a branch with no PR, and an open PR. THE GOOD CASES ARE THE LOAD-BEARING HALF for a destructive instrument. A sweep regressing toward deleting work shows up as a GOOD case scoring BAD, which the harness reports BLIND. MEASURED on 2026-09-28 (issue #1281), three mutations of the gate's classification, each reported BLIND: deleting the `unpushed` skip turns good-unpushed-commit-beyond-merged-head `removable`; deleting the `dirty` skip turns good-dirty `removable`; deleting the `occupied` skip turns good-process-inside-worktree `removable`. The anchor covers the OTHER direction - that the known-bad case can be missed - and is constructed, because the gate has no blind ancestor to vendor. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It runs the DRY-RUN ONLY. `--apply`, the removal-time re-reads of dirt and unpushed state, and worktree-remove.sh's own refusals (claimed, in use, dirty, unpushed) are not exercised here; the classification they act on is. It does not exercise the `@{u}` upstream lane of the unpushed check: no case configures an upstream, so the PR-head comparison - the lane that survives `git fetch --prune`, the normal post-merge state - is the one under test. It does not exercise `locked`, `prunable`, `detached` or the `pr-unknown` / `occupancy-unknown` undecidables; a gate whose undecidable lane stopped reporting would still pass these cases. THE FIXTURE IS BUILT, NEVER THE HOST: a throwaway repository outside every checkout (run-case.sh refuses otherwise), a stub `gh` answering the one PR query the gate makes, and a fake /proc through the gate's FLOW_WORKTREE_SWEEP_PROC_ROOT seam whose PIDs sit above the kernel's maximum pid_max so no real process can collide. The cases name no answer: each fixture.env states facts about the worktree and the discriminator is the gate's own SWEEP_WORKTREE line. UNAVAILABLE IS DECLARED FOR A MISSING git OR bash ONLY (#1117). Since #1171 git is staged into the negative-controls CI step, so this control runs there; the declaration is for a host without it. Every other reason a case cannot run prints `cannot-run`, which matches no declared signal and is therefore reported loudly rather than excused.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, because the gate has never had a blind revision to vendor. It is the gate at 164fdd4 with ONE line changed: the occupancy match `[[ "$cwd" == "$wt"* ]]`, a bare prefix test. That is not an invented defect - the gate's own comment records measuring the collision it causes on a real host (`kyle-issue-1142` is a string prefix of `kyle-issue-1142-container-spec-superseded`), which is why the real test requires the exact path or a `/` after it. MEASURED against every case: the anchor reports the known-bad worktree `skip occupied:pids=9999901` - a process in the SIBLING directory read as occupying it - and so MISSES it, while agreeing with the gate on all five GOOD cases (each skipped for the same reason the gate gives). Its blindness is in the safe direction, which is exactly the one this control's anchor must demonstrate: 'removable=0 because it looked at the wrong thing' printing the same bytes as 'removable=0 because nothing qualified'.
